permissions.description: Choose the server a punishment applies on (server:<name>).
Punish with -S: only the console is told.
Hear when a banned player tries to join.

header: xBans: bans, mutes and warnings, the LiteBans way.
Apply changes with /xbans reload. A bad value falls back to its default with a
warning in the console; xBans never stops over config. The messages are in lang/.

comment: How this plugin's messages look, and the language they're in. shared uses the
setting in plugins/Xena/config.yml, which every Xena plugin reads; anything else is
this plugin's own.
The language players see messages in: auto for each player's own (their client's
language setting), or one language for everyone, such as de or pt-BR.
The language of the console, and of players whose language has no file in lang/.
The look every message shares, used in messages as tags: <prefix>, <highlight>,
<success> and <error>. Colours are names (gray, gold) or hex (#B48CFF), with bold,
italic, underlined, strikethrough or obfuscated if you like: <#B48CFF><bold>.
<prefix> starts the default messages. Make it your server's name, such as
"<dark_gray>[<gradient:#B48CFF:#5EE08A>MyServer</gradient>]</dark_gray> ", or blank for none.
The colour of message text that has no tag of its own.
<highlight>: names and values, such as a player or a speed.
<success>: something turned on or done.
<error>: something refused or turned off.
What punished players see. The screens' words are in lang/.
<appeal> in the screens.
Each command can be turned off (it isn't registered, so another plugin can have its
name), given aliases, or a different permission. xBans takes over vanilla /ban,
/pardon, /ban-ip, /pardon-ip, /kick and /banlist, and gives them back when its own
are off.
Players see their own warnings with this; others' need xbans.warnings.others.
Accounts that share an IP with a player: LiteBans' /dupeip.
How punishing works.
The reason when none is given.
Punishments are silent (-s) unless -p (public) is given.
What a mute blocks besides chat.
Commands a muted player can't use. Aliases and namespaced forms (/essentials:msg) are
blocked too. On Fabric, Minecraft's /me and /say, and zChat's /msg and /reply.
Muted players can't write on signs (Bukkit).
Muted players can't write or sign books (Bukkit).
Muted players can't rename items on an anvil (Bukkit, from 1.11).
How long a warning lasts when /warn isn't given a duration.
Commands the console runs when a player reaches a number of active warnings. <player>
is their name; each key is the count.
Templates: /ban Steve hacking follows the "hacking" template. Each time the same
player gets the same template, the next step of its ladder applies (the last step
repeats). type is ban, mute or warn. A past punishment counts toward the ladder
until expire-ladder has passed since it was made, unless it was revoked. ip makes
it an IP punishment. A template's permission is needed to use it (blank:
xbans.template.<name>); operators have it. Its lengths are held to the sender's
staff-limits like typed ones, unless they have xbans.limit.bypass-templates.
entries.defaultText: {hacking: {type: "ban", reason: "Hacking", ladder: ["1w", "30d", "permanent"], expire-ladder: "180d", ip: false, silent: false, permission: "xbans.template.hacking"}, spam: {type: "mute", reason: "Spamming", ladder: ["1h", "1d", "1w"], expire-ladder: "180d", ip: false, silent: false, permission: "xbans.template.spam"}, language: {type: "warn", reason: "Inappropriate language", ladder: ["30d"], expire-ladder: "180d", ip: false, silent: false, permission: "xbans.template.language"}}

comment: Who can punish whom, and for how long.
Weights: a player with xbans.weight.<n> can only be punished by someone with a higher
weight. Players without one can be punished by anyone with the command. A player's
weight is the one they had when they last joined, if they're offline.
Longest ban and mute each group may give. A staff member with a group's permission
gets its limits; with several, the longest. Staff in no group have none. The
permissions aren't given to operators by default.
IP addresses: for IP bans and mutes, /alts and /iphistory. IP addresses are personal
data: see https://plugins.xenastudios.co/xbans/privacy/
Record players' IPs. Off: no IP bans or mutes, /alts or /iphistory, and nothing is
stored.
Store a salted hash instead of the IP: alts and IP bans still work, but there's no list
of addresses to leak. The salt is in ip-salt.txt in xBans' folder; copy it to every
server of a network (and the proxy), and turn it on with every server stopped. Once on,
it stays on for that database: addresses already stored are hashed. A lost salt: see
the privacy page (reset-ip-salt.txt).
Tell staff when a player joins who shares an IP with a banned account.
Server scopes, for networks: a punishment can apply on every server (global) or on one.
/ban Steve server:survival bans Steve on survival only.
This server's name, for server:<name>. Each server of a network needs its own: the
name the proxy gives it, so the proxy turns a player away from the servers they're
banned on.
global: punishments apply on every server unless server: says otherwise. local: on this one.
Lists: /history, /staffhistory, /warnings, /banlist, /mutelist, /alts.
How dates are written, as in Java's DateTimeFormatter (y M d H h m s a E and
'quoted text'). The server's time zone.
Where this plugin keeps its data. Read at startup only: restart after changing it.
sqlite keeps everything in one file in the plugin's folder, with nothing to set up.
mysql (or MariaDB) is for networks, or servers with a lot of history.
shared keeps it in the database every Xena plugin can share, set in plugins/Xena/config.yml.
Put in front of every table's name, so plugins and servers can share one database.
Only for type: mysql.
Extra connection settings, as in a JDBC URL: useSSL=true&serverTimezone=UTC.
The connections used to read, beside the one that writes.
How many: 0 picks for the database (1 for SQLite, 2 for MySQL). More helps only a
MySQL server that many reads wait on.
Network mode: a ban made on one server kicks the player from the others and reaches
their ban lists within check-every seconds; with xBans on the proxy too, a banned
player can't get onto the network at all. Every server and the proxy share one MySQL or
MariaDB database (storage) for it. Read at startup and on reload.
On when several servers share this plugin's MySQL or MariaDB database, so a change
made on one (a ban, a mute) reaches the others within a few seconds.
Leave it off for a single server: it does nothing on SQLite.
Seconds between checks for the other servers' changes.
Telling you when a newer version is out: in the console, and to players with
<plugin>.admin.update when they join. Asks Modrinth once a day, off the server's threads,
sending only the plugin's version, the platform and the Minecraft version.
Whether to ask at all.
Which releases to hear of: release, beta (betas and releases) or alpha (everything).
Under a long list in chat (/homes, /history, ...) when it has more than one page.
<previous> and <next> are the list's command for those pages; what's inside
<has_previous>...</has_previous> or <has_next>...</has_next> shows only when there's such a page.
In the console, and to players with <plugin>.admin.update as they join, when a newer version is out
on the update channel the config picks. <url> is its download page.
/<plugin> debug, before the health checks' results.
/<plugin> debug: the database answered. <database> is where it is, such as "MySQL at db:3306/minecraft".
/<plugin> debug: the database didn't answer. <reason> is the driver's, in English.
/<plugin> debug: every plugin or mod it depends on is there. <names> lists them, or says none.

messages.english: <gold>!</gold> Dependencies: <names> not installed, so what needs them is off.
comment: /<plugin> debug: optional plugins or mods that aren't installed.
/<plugin> debug: plugins or mods it needs that aren't installed.

messages.english: <success>✔</success> Threads: tasks run where they should (<threading>).
comment: /<plugin> debug: a task on the global thread and one off it each ran where it should.
<threading> is how the server runs work, in English: "Folia's regions", "one main thread".
/<plugin> debug: a task ran on the wrong thread, or didn't run. <reason> is in English.
/<plugin> debug: the config and language files had nothing wrong when they were last read.
/<plugin> debug: problems found the last time the files were read; the console and the report have them all.
/<plugin> debug: every module the config turns on is running.
/<plugin> debug: modules that failed. The report says why.
/<plugin> debug: a check that didn't finish. <check> is its name and <reason> why, in English.

messages.english: <prefix>Debug report: <click:open_url:'<url>'><hover:show_text:'Open it'><highlight><url></highlight></hover></click>. Share this link when asking for help; passwords and tokens are removed.
comment: /<plugin> debug: the report's link at a paste service (mclo.gs).

messages.english: <prefix>Couldn't upload the debug report (<reason>), so it's in <highlight><file></highlight> in the plugin's folder.
comment: /<plugin> debug: the upload failed, so the report was written to a file. <reason> is in English.

messages.english: <prefix>Debug report saved as <highlight><file></highlight> in the plugin's folder.
comment: /<plugin> debug, when uploading is turned off.
/<plugin> debug: the report couldn't be uploaded or written. <reason> is in English.
/<plugin> import: the other plugin's files or tables weren't found.

messages.english: <prefix><error>An import is already running; wait for it to finish.</error>
comment: /<plugin> import while one is running.

messages.english: <prefix>Dry run from <source>: <highlight><importable></highlight> of <total> records would be imported, <skipped> skipped. Nothing was changed.
comment: /<plugin> import <source> --dry-run: what a real run would do.
/<plugin> import: the run starts.

messages.english: <prefix>Carrying on the import from <source> where it stopped, after <done> of <total> records...
comment: /<plugin> import: a run that stopped before is carried on.
/<plugin> import: progress, every few seconds.
/<plugin> import: one record that failed. The import carries on; the console lists them all.
/<plugin> import: the run finished.

messages.english: <prefix><error>The import from <source> stopped: <reason></error> Run it again to carry on where it left off.
comment: /<plugin> import: the run stopped, such as when the other plugin's database went away. <reason> is in English.
/<plugin> migrate to the storage type in use.

messages.english: <prefix><error>A migration is already running; wait for it to finish.</error>
comment: /<plugin> migrate while one is running.

messages.english: <prefix><error>The <type> database already has data (<tables>).</error> Add --force to replace it with this server's.
comment: /<plugin> migrate: the target isn't empty. <tables> lists its tables with their rows.
/<plugin> migrate: the copy starts.
/<plugin> migrate: one table is copied.

messages.english: <prefix><success>Moved the data to <type> and checked it (rows: <rows>).</success> The plugin now uses <type>.
comment: /<plugin> migrate: done; the config's storage type was changed and applied.

messages.english: <prefix><error>Moving the data to <type> failed: <reason></error> The plugin still uses <from>.
comment: /<plugin> migrate: it failed, and the storage type wasn't changed. <reason> is in English.
/<plugin> forget: the name isn't one the server knows. A UUID works too.
/<plugin> forget: done.

messages.english: <prefix><error>Some of <player>'s data couldn't be deleted (<failed>).</error> Records deleted: <records>. Run it again.
comment: /<plugin> forget: part of it failed. <failed> lists what, with why, in English.
/<plugin> reload: config.yml and the language files were read again and applied.
What's inside <has_one>...</has_one> shows when one module is on, <has_many>...</has_many> otherwise.
/<plugin> reload: one line per problem found in the files, in English. The console has them too.
/<plugin> reload: a module that failed, and why, in English.

messages.english: <prefix><error>Reloading <plugin> failed; the console has the details.
comment: /<plugin> reload: something went wrong; the settings from before are still in use.
Rare: a command that went away as it was typed.

messages.english: <prefix><error>You don't have permission to do that.
comment: The sender lacks the command's permission.
The console or a command block ran a command only players can use.
The command was typed with missing or extra words. <usage> is how to type it.
No player the sender can see is online by the name typed (<player>).
A number was expected. <input> is what was typed.
A whole number was expected. <input> is what was typed.
A number below the least the command takes (<min>).
A number above the most the command takes (<max>).
A word that isn't one of those the command takes (<choices>, comma-separated).
What was typed can't be used: true or false, a length of time, a name. <reason> is in English.
The command has a cooldown. <time> is how long is left.
A command that needs confirming, such as forget. <line> is the command, <time> how long there is.

messages.english: <prefix><error>Something went wrong running that command; the console has the details.
comment: The command hit an error. The console has what happened.

messages.english: <prefix>xBans <highlight><version></highlight> on <platform>, with <count> bans and mutes in force from <storage>. <gray>/xbans reload | debug | import
comment: /xbans on its own.

messages.english:
<#FF6B6B><bold>You are banned from this server.</bold>

<gray>Reason: <white><reason>

<gray>Appeal at <white><appeal></white>
<dark_gray>ID #<id>
comment: What punished players see. <reason>, <staff>, <id>, <expires> (a date), <time-left>,
<duration> and <appeal> (screens.appeal-link in config.yml) work in each.
A permanent ban, shown when they're kicked and each time they try to join.

messages.english:
<#FF6B6B><bold>You are banned from this server.</bold>

<gray>Reason: <white><reason>
<gray>Ends in <white><time-left></white> (<expires>)

<gray>Appeal at <white><appeal></white>
<dark_gray>ID #<id>

<#FF6B6B><bold>Your IP is banned from this server.</bold>

<gray>Reason: <white><reason>
<gray>Ends: <white><expires>

<gray>Appeal at <white><appeal></white>
<dark_gray>ID #<id>
comment: A ban on their IP rather than their account.

messages.english:
<#EB2F4A>The server is still starting.</#EB2F4A>
<gray>Try again in a few seconds.
comment: Shown when they can't join because xBans is still loading its bans (only in the first
seconds after a start, or while the database can't be reached at startup).
Told to a muted player who tries to chat.
Told to a player when they're muted, warned or unmuted, if they're online.
Told to the server when someone is punished. <player>, <staff>, <reason>, <duration>
("for 7d" or "permanently", from the words below) and <id>. Silent punishments (-s)
go only to staff with xbans.notify.silent, with silent-prefix in front.
<staff> is who lifted it.
Put after the theme's <prefix> of a silent punishment's broadcast.
<duration> for a permanent punishment, and for one with an end (<time> is how long).

messages.english: <prefix><highlight><player></highlight> tried to join but is banned: <reason>
comment: Told to staff with xbans.notify.banned-join when a banned player tries to join. <player>,
<reason>. Blank for none.
Told to staff with xbans.notify.alts when a player joins who shares an IP with a banned
account. <player>, and <alts>: the banned accounts. Blank for none.

messages.english: <prefix><error>xBans is still opening its database.</error> Try again in a moment.
comment: xBans is still opening its database, just after a start.
<player> is the name typed.
<player>'s IP isn't known (they haven't joined since IPs were recorded).

messages.english: <prefix><error>IP punishments are off on this server.
comment: IP commands are off because ips.enabled is false.

messages.english: <prefix><error><highlight><input></highlight> isn't a length of time.</error> Use 30m, 1d12h, 2mo or perm.
comment: <input> isn't a length of time.

messages.english: <prefix><error><highlight><player></highlight> is already banned until <expires>.</error> Unban them first to shorten it.
comment: <player> is already banned or muted, longer than this would. <expires> is when it ends.

messages.english: <prefix><error><highlight><player></highlight> is already muted until <expires>.</error> Unmute them first to shorten it.
<prefix><error>There's no punishment <highlight>#<id></highlight> to do that to.
comment: <id> isn't a punishment, or isn't one this command can revoke.
<player> has xbans.exempt.
<player>'s weight (xbans.weight.<n>) is as high as the sender's or higher.

messages.english: <prefix><error>That was given by someone who outranks you.</error> <dark_gray>#<id>
comment: Revoking a punishment made by someone whose weight was higher than the sender's (the
console's is highest), or replacing one with a ban or mute that's no longer. Staff can
always revoke their own; xbans.unban.override revokes any. <player>, <expires>, <id>.
Over the sender's staff-limits. <max> is the longest they may give.

messages.english: <prefix><error>The <highlight><template></highlight> template's next step is permanent, so it needs /ban or /mute.
comment: /tempban or /tempmute with a template whose next step is permanent. <template> is its name.
A template's permission is missing. <template> is its name.
Choosing a server: needs xbans.scope.
Another plugin stopped the punishment.

messages.english: <prefix><error>That couldn't be saved.</error> The console says why.
comment: Couldn't be saved. The console says why.
/prunehistory. <count> entries of <player>'s were removed.

messages.english: <prefix>That removes <highlight><count></highlight> inactive entries from <player>'s history for good. Run it again with <highlight>confirm</highlight> on the end.
comment: /prunehistory without confirming. <count> would be removed.
/history and /staffhistory. <player>, <count>.
One punishment in a list. <id>, <date>, <type> (from types below), <player>, <staff>,
<reason>, <length> ("7d", "permanent"), <status> (from the words below), <scope>.
Under a list when it has more pages.
<status> words. <time> is how long is left; <staff> who revoked it.
<type> words.

messages.english: <prefix><highlight><player></highlight> has nothing active of that kind.
comment: /checkban and /checkmute: a line per active one, then its details.
/warnings. <player>, <count> active.
/banlist and /mutelist. <count> on this server.
/alts. <player>, <count>. Each account: <name>, with <state> from alt-states (banned,
muted, online or offline).
/iphistory. <player>, <count>. Each line: <ip>, <first>, <last> (dates).

messages.english: <prefix>Found in <highlight><source></highlight>: <bans> bans, <mutes> mutes, <warnings> warnings, <kicks> kicks and <players> players. Nothing was imported yet: run it again with <highlight>confirm</highlight> on the end.
comment: A dry run. <source>, <bans>, <mutes>, <warnings>, <kicks>, <players> found.
<source>, <added> new punishments, <skipped> already imported.
<reason> it couldn't, in English.

messages.english: <prefix><highlight><count></highlight> wildcard IP bans (such as 192.168.1.*) aren't imported: xBans bans whole addresses only.
comment: A dry run or an import that found LiteBans wildcard IP bans (192.168.1.*), which aren't imported. <count>.
LiteBans' H2 or AdvancedBan's HSQLDB file, read from a copy with a driver fetched for it (downloaded once into plugins/Xena/libraries/). <file>, <driver>.

messages.english: <prefix><error><source> is still using <file>.</error> Stop it first: move its jar out of the plugins folder (keep its folder), restart, then import again.
comment: <source>'s database file <file> is open: the plugin is running, here or on another server.
<reason>, in English, says why and which jar to put where to import without a download. <driver>, <file>.
<sources>: the ones xBans knows.

messages.english: <prefix>xBans <highlight><version></highlight> on <platform>: <count> bans in force from <storage>, enforced at the proxy's login. <gray>/xbansproxy reload | debug
comment: /xbansproxy on the proxy. <storage>: the database, and whether the servers share it.

events.description: A punishment is about to be made, after every check. Cancel it to stop it.
